summary: A survey of junk forensic science in the US, from overstated fingerprint matching to bite mark analysis, corpse dowsing, clothing-wrinkle matching and 911-call analysis, and the innocent people convicted on it.

evidence.note: Faulds and fingerprint history from the 1870s-1880 opens the historical survey
1974 nose-bite case leads to People v. Marx, foundational bite mark ruling
Mayfield wrongly tied by FBI to the 2004 Madrid train bombing
1982 Virginia rape and murder case; Harward convicted on bite marks
hair microscopy convicts Mark Reid, a Black man; racial classification of hair
Mississippi dentist Michael West fabricates bite marks on bodies
Arpad Vass sells dowsing-based corpse finder to grieving families
Harpster 911-call analysis still taught to police at release

notes: Survey of a practice, so no roles. Theme primary could arguably be policing-incarceration; chose quackery-pseudoscience as the pitch is that the techniques are junk science. Levine, West and Vass birth/death years not stated, so floruit used. Covered span starts with 19th-century fingerprint origins (about 5 minutes). Main span end null as the practices remain in use.
